title: zero-trust-controlplane-egress-bastion-bridge-and-dns-stitcher
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: add a hardened zero-trust egress path for control plane VPCs that (1) provides an auditable, tenant-isolated bastion bridge for outbound control-plane management traffic, (2) implements cross-account delegated DNS stitching for control-plane endpoints, and (3) exposes an operator-safe toggle for progressive rollouts and immediate rollback. This PR bundles Terraform module changes (networking and iam), Helm chart hooks for the installer control-plane agent, and an upgrade/rollback hook for the private-installer operator. Implementation summary: - Terraform: introduce module vpc/egress_bastion_bridge. Creates a pair of AZ-aware bastion ENIs in a dedicated egress subnet with sg rules restricted to control-plane CIDRs and a proxy IAM role for signed egress requests. Adds route table association and optional Transit Gateway/Peering attachment ACLs. Adds a cross-account Route53 delegation resource (hosted zone delegation + glue) with conditional IAM assume-role to allow control plane to provision endpoint records in customer-owned zones. - Helm: add pre-upgrade/post-upgrade hooks to install a small controlplane-egress-agent DaemonSet that performs signed TLS-forwarding to the bastion bridge, emits metrics to the console (egress.latency, egress.errors), and can be disabled via values.egress.enabled=false. - Installer operator: adds a reconcile step and feature-flag to orchestrate staged promotion of DNS delegation and egress-bastion creation; supports a canary rollout using tag-based subnet selectors. - Tests and validation: end-to-end terraform plan/apply smoke in the lab (benchmark-lab), integration test that the installer can create a delegated record and validate DNS resolution from a control plane pod, and unit tests for the IAM policy templating. Rollout plan: 1) Enable feature-flag in staging clusters, 2) Create cross-account delegation in a single region and monitor DNS propagation metrics and egress latency for 48h, 3) Promote to all regions with automated remediation steps. Revert plan: operator exposes 'egress.disable' annotation to short-circuit agent; terraform destroy plan created as part of the PR for emergency teardown. Security notes: minimal IAM permissions are requested and documented in SECURITY.md; bastion ENIs are locked down to the control plane CIDR and central ops role. Backwards compatibility: default flags are off; customers must opt-in to enable delegation and bastion bridge. This description includes implementation details, testing notes, rollout and rollback instructions, and security rationale.
